Laatgotische hallenkerk, begonnen in de: Late Gothic hall church, begun in the 15th century, with the largest stained-glass windows in the country
Scheve toren van de afgebroken Onze-Liev: Leaning tower of the demolished Church of Our Lady, with a carillon that plays every quarter hour
Stadhuis in Lodewijk XIV-stijl uit 1737,: Town hall in Louis XIV style from 1737, by master builder Jacob Jongh
The oldest stone house in Edam, from c. 1540, with a floating cellar
Waaggebouw uit 1778 aan de Kaasmarkt, wa: Weigh house from 1778 on the cheese market square, where the cheese market is held on summer Wednesdays
Evangelisch-lutherse kerk uit 1739-1741,: Evangelical Lutheran church from 1739-1741 with Louis XIV facades, now the Protestant church De Swaen
In 1555 gesticht als tehuis voor ouderen: Founded in 1555 as a home for elderly people who bought their way in; the buildings are 17th and 18th century
Een schuilkerkje aan de Kaasmarkt uit 17: A hidden church on the cheese market square from 1702: Mennonites were allowed to meet in the Dutch Republic, but their church was not allowed to look like one from the outside.
Het weeshuis van Edam aan de Kaasmarkt,: Edam's orphanage on the cheese market square, built in the last quarter of the 19th century on the site of its predecessor.
Fort van de Stelling van Amsterdam, gebo: Fort of the Defence Line of Amsterdam, built 1908-1913, world heritage
Het huis van de sluiswachter bij de zees: The lock keeper's house at the sea lock in the Oorgat. Behind it stands a stone post marking how high the water rose in January 1916, when the Zuiderzee came over the dikes.
Hotel-restaurant in een rij 17e-eeuwse h: Hotel and restaurant in a row of 17th-century houses on the water of the Spuistraat, with a garden on the canal.
Het hart van Edam: de dam in het riviert: The heart of Edam: the dam in the little river IJe (or E) that gave the town its name around 1230. The town hall and the Edams Museum stand on the square.
De schutsluis onder het Damplein, uit 17: The lock under the Damplein, from 1795-1798, separates the water of the Voorhaven from the canals and the polder behind it.
Een smalle houten ophaalbrug over de Sch: A narrow wooden drawbridge over the canal by the Schepenmakersdijk, just wide enough for a pedestrian. It is one of the most photographed spots in Edam.
Een stenen paal achter de sluiswachtersw: A stone post behind the lock keeper's house in the Oorgat with the level of the storm surge of 13 and 14 January 1916, which flooded the Waterland region and led to the building of the Afsluitdijk.
De sluis waarmee de Voorhaven van Edam a: The lock that links Edam's Voorhaven to the IJsselmeer. As early as 1357, with its town charter, Edam was allowed to make a harbour to the sea here.
De overblijfselen van de stadswallen van: The remains of Edam's town walls, the Wester- and Noordervesting, with the moat in front. The fortifications enclosed the town from the 16th century; the Purmerpoort gate was demolished in 1835.
Het strandje van Edam aan het IJsselmeer: Edam's little beach on the IJsselmeer, with steps down the dike and a view across to Marken.
De jachthaven buiten de dijk, waar de Vo: The marina outside the dike, where the Voorhaven reaches the IJsselmeer through the Oorgat.
Jan Nieuwenhuyzen (1724-1806), doopsgezi: Jan Nieuwenhuyzen (1724-1806), Mennonite minister in Edam, founded the Society for Public Welfare (Maatschappij tot Nut van 't Algemeen) here in 1784, which set up schools and libraries for ordinary people. The cheese market square bears his name.
De Joodse begraafplaats van Edam aan de: Edam's Jewish cemetery on the edge of the old town, by the Oosterkade. Next to it stands the memorial De tochtgenoten for the Jewish people of Edam deported in the war.
Rachel beweent haar kinderen: een gedenk: Rachel weeping for her children: a memorial by the Jewish cemetery for the Jewish inhabitants of Edam who did not survive the war.
Hier reed van 1888 tot 1932 de stoomtram: From 1888 to 1932 the steam tram from Amsterdam to Edam ran here; the line is now a cycle path along the fortifications.
De dijk tussen Edam en de polder Zeevang: The dike between Edam and the Zeevang polder and the IJsselmeer, no longer sea but a lake since 1932. The Zuiderzeepad trail runs along it.
Edam begint als een dam in het veenrivie: Edam begins as a dam in the little peat river IJe, also called the E, which flowed into the Zuiderzee here. Around 1230 the inlets of the Waterland are dammed, and a settlement of fishermen and traders grows at the dam: IJedam, later Edam.
Op 18 mei 1737 legt Roelof Boot de eerst: On 18 May 1737 Roelof Boot lays the first stone of the new town hall on the Damplein, designed by Jacob Jongh in Louis XIV style, with a sandstone entrance under the town arms. Inside hangs the painted wallpaper by Willem Rave from 1738. Today the tourist office is downstairs and Edam still holds its weddings here.
Aan de Voorhaven bouwen de lutheranen in: On the Voorhaven the Lutherans build their own church in 1739-1741, with facades in Louis XIV style. It is one of Edam's 176 national monuments.
Onder het Damplein ligt de Damsluis uit: Under the Damplein lies the Damsluis of 1795-1798, which separates the water of the Voorhaven from the canals and the polders. Well into the 19th century the Zuiderzee could push the groundwater up to here at high tide.
In 1357 krijgt Edam stadsrechten van gra: In 1357 Edam receives its town charter from Count William V, with the right to dig two new harbours to the sea: the Voorhaven and the Oorgat. Shipbuilding, herring fishing and the cheese trade bring the town prosperity in the centuries that follow. In 1544 Charles V orders the open link to the Zuiderzee closed; in 1570 the people of Edam smash the lock gates again.
In de nacht van 13 op 14 januari 1916 ja: In the night of 13 to 14 January 1916 a north-westerly storm drives the Zuiderzee over the dikes of the Waterland. Behind the lock keeper's house in the Oorgat stands a stone post with the level of that night. The disaster led to the Afsluitdijk; since 1932 Edam has lain on a lake.
Het laatste fort van de Stelling van Ams: The last fort of the Defence Line of Amsterdam, built 1908-1913 at the Oorgat to cover the sea dike and the lock. It was manned in the First World War, used by the Wehrmacht in the Second, and held weapons and ammunition until 1980. Since 2005 a foundation keeps it open; the Defence Line is world heritage.
Trijntje Cornelisdochter Keever wordt in: Trijntje Cornelisdochter Keever is born in Edam in April 1616 and grows to be possibly the tallest woman who ever lived: 2.54 metres. Her parents show her at fairs. She dies in 1633, seventeen years old, and is buried in the Grote Kerk. Her life-size portrait hangs in the Edams Museum.
In de nieuwe stadsuitbreiding aan de noo: In the new northern extension of the town, the Grote or St Nicholas Church rises in the 15th century, one of the largest hall churches in the country. After a fire in 1602 come the famous stained-glass windows, donated by towns and wealthy families. In 1699 lightning strikes the spire; the tower stayed low after that.
Edam was een vestingstadje: de Wester- e: Edam was a fortified town: the Wester- and Noordervesting with their ramparts and moat are still there. The Purmerpoort, the town gate on the west side, was demolished in 1835. The mermaid of Edam, the statue that adorned the gate, can now be seen in the Edams Museum.
In 1555 gesticht als tehuis voor ouderen: Founded in 1555 as a home for elderly people who bought their way in with money or goods, the proveniers. The present buildings on the J.C. Brouwersgracht are 17th and 18th century and stand around a quiet inner garden.
Op 16 april 1526 geeft Karel V Edam het: On 16 April 1526 Charles V grants Edam the right to a free weekly market and a weigh house. In 1574 William of Orange makes that right perpetual, as thanks for help at the relief of Alkmaar. For centuries Edam cheese was traded here, until 1922. Since 1989 there is a cheese market again every Wednesday morning in July and August, with cheese carriers and cheese girls.
De oudste kern van het stadje ligt rond: The oldest core of the town lies around the Church of Our Lady, the Kleine Kerk, founded in 1310. The church was demolished in 1883; only the tower with its 16th-century octagonal lantern remained. During work in 1972 it threatened to fall and was shored up, but it has leaned ever since. The carillon plays every quarter hour.
Een smal houten ophaalbruggetje, een kwa: A narrow wooden drawbridge, a kwakel, over the water by the Doelland. The bridge is a national monument and one of the most photographed spots in the town.
Het oudste stenen huis van Edam, gebouwd: The oldest stone house in Edam, built around 1540 for a merchant, has a cellar that floats loose from the house on the groundwater and moves with its level. The town bought the house at auction in 1893, had Pierre Cuypers restore it and opened the Edams Museum in it in 1895. In 1962 it was the model for KLM's Delft blue house.
De binnenstad binnen de oude vesting is: The old town within the former fortifications is a protected townscape, with 176 national monuments. Edam celebrated 650 years of its town charter in 2007. End of the tour.
Het laatste fort van de Stelling van Ams: The last fort of the Defence Line of Amsterdam, built 1908-1913 at the Oorgat to cover the sea dike and the lock: a bomb-proof building under an earthen rampart, with a moat around it. Since 2005 a foundation keeps it open to visitors.
